newsitem.title: JORDAN: Egypt's envoy resumes mission to Israel on Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's envoy resumes mission to Israel on Sunday.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said his senior adviser Osama el-Baz would return to Israel on Sunday to resume a mission "without preconditions" to try to break a deadlock in Israeli-Palestinian peace talks.

"My personal envoy was with them (Israel) and he will go tomorrow again and we will see what they will reach and what direction can be taken so that the Palestinian-Israeli sides can continue talks," Mubarak, accompanied by Jordan's King Hussein, told reporters after talks in Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba.
The Egyptian envoy flew to Israel on Friday and talked with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to pave the way for the two leaders to meet on Tuesday at the Egyptian Red Sea resort of Sharm el-Sheikh.

Mubarak, whose talks with King Hussein covered reviving the stalled peace talks, brushed aside suggestions that Egypt had demanded that Israel halt construction of Jewish settlements as a precondition for resuming talks.
"We have not talked about conditions, we are talking about how to solve the present crisis, we cannot say preconditions," Mubarak said.

Egypt's Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said in broadcast remarks on Friday that the Israeli-Egyptian summit would succeed if Israel agreed to stop building settlements for Jews on lands captured in the 1967 Middle East war.
Egypt, partner to a 1979 treaty with Israel, hopes to break an Israel-PLO peacemaking deadlock.
Mubarak has previously proposed a six-month Israeli freeze on settlement expansion. Netanyahu vows his 11-month-old government will press ahead with construction.

Palestinians say stalled talks can resume only when Israel halts work on the settlement in East Jerusalem. Netanyahu plunged negotiations with the PLO into crisis two months ago when he broke ground on the settlement.
